heading: What I’m working on
lede: Three questions I’m actively thinking about. Each is open to collaboration.
introduction: If you’d like to work together on any of these questions,

topics.label: Quantum algorithms & learning
topics.title: Quantum algorithms and learning
topics.question: Where does a quantum advantage survive the cost of getting data in and answers out?
topics.description: My theoretical work connects quantum linear algebra, open-system dynamics and learning. I want to understand which structures make an algorithm useful, and what limited measurements can tell us about quantum systems.
topics.homeSummary: I develop dissipative algorithms and quantum linear algebra methods, and study how efficiently we can learn quantum dynamics from limited data.

topics.label: AI-assisted algorithm design
topics.title: AI-assisted classical–quantum co-design
topics.question: Can we reduce quantum costs by redesigning the classical work around them?
topics.description: I’m exploring how AI can help choose problem representations, classical preprocessing and quantum implementations together. My starting points are quantum simulation and matrix operations, with costs counted across the full computation.
topics.homeSummary: Quantum algorithms are shaped by the representations and classical computations around them. I want AI to search across these choices and invent new methods, starting with quantum simulation and linear algebra.

topics.label: Scientific agents
topics.title: Scientific agents with checkable results
topics.question: How do we turn an agent’s promising idea into a result another researcher can check?
topics.description: I’m interested in agents that choose what to investigate, use scientific tools and learn from unsuccessful attempts. Quantum-Harbor and QIQCBench are a starting point: agents work in virtual quantum-engineering laboratories, their actions are recorded, and their conclusions are verified independently.
topics.homeSummary: I’m building toward agents that invent methods and pursue scientific questions, starting with classical–quantum co-design and quantum-engineering environments.

perspective.title: Toward QuantumAGI
perspective.text: I’m interested in QuantumAGI as a long-term possibility: how quantum systems could contribute to general intelligence, and how AI could change the way we develop and use quantum computation.

community.title: QIQCOP
community.text: Through QIQCOP, I’m exploring new ways to share open problems and collaborate.
